title.narrative: Geneva Centre for Sector Governance, Accountability in Zambia Police, 2024-2027
Geneva Centre for Sector Governance, reformering av Zambia Police 2024-2027

description.narrative:
While there are a range of interconnected issues influencing policing and police reform in Zambia that need to be addressed, the DCAF/SACCORD programme will focus on three core problems: 1) excessive use of force by the police when facilitating public assemblies, 2) corruption influencing all elements of effectiveness and efficiency of the police, and 3) inefficient policing management limits the extent to which police are responsive to the police to community needs and threats faced by the community.
The overall goal is that the Zambia Police Service promotes a more peaceful and democratic society by upholding and protecting fundamental human rights. The intervention will facilitate an interaction between demand-side pressures for policing reform (in Zambia's civil society, legislative and executive institutions as well as ordinary citizens) and reform work from within the Zambian Police Service itself.
This will require that the programme achieves four Main Outcomes: Outcome 1: The Zambian Police use more proportional and minimal force when dealing with public assemblies, investigations and other routine policing duties. Outcome 2: The Zambian Police systematically seek to facilitate, protect and respect the fundamental right to public assemblies, including during elections. Outcome 3: The Zambian Police are held to account for use of force and corruption with more wide-ranging and systematic reporting and investigations of such incidence. Outcome 4: The Zambian Police apply a more people-centered policing model that seeks to shape operational priorities based on needs expressed by communities, be more responsive and professional in dealing with the community, and be more proactive in communication and outreach to communities.
In order to avoid the pitfalls of "quick results/back to default" as far as institutional changes in ZPS is concerned, and based on previous insights into how changes can happen within the ZPS, DCAF and SACCORD have developed Intermediary Outcomes to be able to track small changes in the internal workings of ZPS that will indicate they are moving forward according to the change path anticipated.
For Outcome 1, the two intermediary outcomes are: - Intermediary Outcome: police begin systematically recording, reporting and justifying any use of force incidence; - Intermediary Outcome: internal and external oversight bodies more systematically and comprehensively investigate and review cases of use of force by the police.
For Outcome 2, the two intermediary outcomes are: - Police systematically undertake steps to analyse risks and create a robust plan for each assembly (apply precaution principle) showcasing a more effective system of management for assemblies; - In all cases where there is a restriction on any assembly the police duly justify such restrictions and offer reasonable corrective measures to allow the assembly to proceed.
For Outcome 3, the three intermediary outcomes are: - The public more readily reports (or processes complaints) against the police concerning cases of police corruption; - The frequency and number of investigations of police corruption are increased with more proactive actions by both internal and external oversight bodies to tackle corruption within the police; - Police apply different models (operational strategies) and management safeguards that reduce the risks of police corruption.
For Outcome 4, the four intermediary outcomes are: - The number of women seeking promotion to senior ranks is increased; - The police utilise analysis and information (including data from performance management systems) to prioritise how and which threats to tackle; - The police have underlying policies and internal regulations which reflect a normative and value commitment to people-centered policing; - The police are more active in preventive policing and conflict mediation operations in communities.

The focus of the programme is to help make the Zambian Police more accountable and responsive and that they will apply a more human rights ­based approach to policing in line with democratic policing standards. Activities will be based on three pillars: Pillar 1: Improved Accountability of the Police Pillar 2: More Efficient Management of the Police Pillar 3: Enhanced Management of Elections by the Police
